notes_for_editor: Thin record. NHLR says little is known. The only substantive source is an urban-exploration photo tour (Abandoned in 360, August 2025) that uses hedged language ('likely', 'perhaps') and gives a 1953 completion, a Florida Forest Service builder and a guessed 100 ft height; those are attributed in the story and not put in facts as verified. The mid-2000s closure (the article's only dated support for it is a wall map marked Spring/Summer 2008), the 1999 tower count and the staffing narrative in that article are not used as facts; the story attributes the closure to the photo tour. The link between the NHLR 'Marion County Airfield' tower and the photo tour's Dunnellon Ranger Station is inferred from names and location; no page says they are one structure. Museum of Florida History returned HTTP 500 and floridamemory.com returned 403; not retried. Access, visit and staffing are unknown and left out of facts. NHLR credits a photo to David Viero, but the image and licence were not checked, so no photo entry was added. Two web searches were used. Fact-check 2026-10-08: story now says registered (NHLR 'Date Registered', not accepted), gives the Dunnellon Army Air Field as the name the field was known by, and attributes the mid-2000s closure to the photo tour without implying a record.
